full_judgment:
Mr. Syed A.B. Mahmudul Huq J:- This rule was issued on 21.12.08 calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the delay of 2050 days in filling the appeal against the order dated 19.10.2002 passed by the Joint District Judge and Arbitrator, Dhaka in Arbitration Case No.231 of 1980 should not be condoned. 

 2. In the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, the petitioner has explained the delay of 2050 days, stating that the suit land was acquired by the Government in L.A. Case No.2026 of 1968 and the possession thereof was taken over by the government on 21.6.68. On 9.5.80, the respondent filed an application for release of the property. The property was de-requisitioned in favour of the owner and the government handed over the possession thereof to Mr. A.Y. Maoshiuzzaman, son of the petitioner for derequisition. 

 3. The property was acquired for the Music Collage and the rent was fixed at TkAl2.50 per month. The respondent filed an Arbitration Suit No.231 of 1980 in the Arbitration Tribunal, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rents. Then on 19.10.02, the Arbitration Court gave an award for Tk.64,53,136/- in favour of the owner. The government preferred Appeal No.01 of 2006, from the said award before the learned District Judge, Dhaka, although the appeal was to be filed before the Hon'ble High Court Division under Section 7(0 of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948. The owner of the Property, the respondent opposite party filed Civil Revision No.4400 of 2006 in the High Court Division on 17.05.07 and obtained Rule and the rule was made absolute by this Division, setting aside the judgment and order dated 24.08.06, passed by the Court of Appeal below in Arbitration Appeal No.01 of 2006, which admitted the appeal condoning the delay therein. Thereafter, the respondent owner of the property put the award in Execution in Money Execution Case No.03 of 2005 in the Court of Arbitration Tribunal. In which case, a show cause notice was issued upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and order attaching the car and other Properties of Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was passed. The Money Execution case is pending. In the supplementary Affidavit dated 05.11.08, the appellant explained the delay stating further that after traveling in wrong forum, while the rule in C.R. No.4400 of 2006 was absolute on 17.5.2007, a proposal for filing a Miscellaneous appeal from the Judgment dated 19.10.2002 of the Arbitration Case No.23I of 1980, was made on 24.3.2008 by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka. The Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, formed a committee for causing investigation about the facts of filing the appeal before learned District Judge and the committee is functioning. After receiving the proposal dated 24.03.08, for filing the appeal, the Solicitor on 24.04.08, approved the proposal and transmitted the record of the case to the Attorney General's office on 27.04.08 for filing the appeal. The office of the Attorney General received the record and Mrs. Nahid Yeasmin. learned D.A.G. endorsed the some file to Mr. Md. Shakatul Hoque, learned A.A.G. and requesting him to prepare a Memo of appeal within 10 days and the Memo of appeal was drafted on 25.05.08 and was filed on 01.6.08 and it was found from a report that the appeal was out of time by 2050 days. It has been stated that there was no latches or negligence on the part of the appellant and the delay of 2050 days was prayed to be condoned under Section 5 of the Limitation Act. 

 6. On the other hand Mr. A.Y. Mashiuzzaman, the learned Advocate for the opposite party referring to the Counter Affidavit, submits that from the award there lies an appeal under Section 7(f) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, and the forum is the High Court Division and he submits that a time limit has been prescribed for filing an appeal under Rule 9(16) of (Emergency) Requisition Rules, which is 60 days. He submits that the respondent as petitioner preferred a Civil Revision against the order passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka admitting the appeal on condoning the delay of 1387 days, and the rule was made absolute on contest against the appellant and the impugned order was set aside, and the plea of prosecuting the appeal in wrong forum, for 2050 days is not in accordance with law as provided in the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act. He submits that under Section 7(t) of the said Act, appeal has to be filed in the High Court Division against an award of Arbitrator and he then submits that under Rule 9(16) of (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, the appeal has to be filed within 60 days of the receipt of the notice of award under sub rule 14, and he cited a case reported in 43 DLR (AD) 28, in support of his submission about special limitation and he finally submits that the appeal was a time barred appeal, and it was filed not in the proper forum as per section 7(f) of the Act and was filed beyond the time limit and the limitation having been prescribed under Rule 9(16) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, the delay cannot be condoned. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocate of the parties and perused the application for condo nation and the Supplementary Affidavit in support of the application dated 05.11.08, the counter Affidavit filed by the Defendant party and the original memo of Appeal containing the impugned order. The impugned order was passed on 19.10.02, by the learned Joint District Judge and Arbitration Court, Dhaka in Arbitration Case No.231 of 1980. It is an award passed in Arbitration case and under Section 7(f) of the Act an appeal against the award of Arbitrator lies in the High Court Division and under Rule 9(16), an appeal against an award of Arbitrator shall be preferred within 60 days of the receipt of the notice by the parties as referred to in sub rule 14. 

 8. We have gone through the case of Isaque (Md.) Vs. Government of Bangladesh, reported in 43 DLR(AD) 28. In this case it has been held that appellate Court is not empowered to condone the delay in time barred appeal under section 5 of the Limitation Act, in view of clear provision of Section 29(2) which excludes application of Section 5. 

 9. In the case, we find the award was passed by the Arbitrator and appeal there from lies to the High Court Division and there is a special limitation provided under the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Rules, 1948 for preferring appeal, that is 60 days, and relying on the decision reported is 43 DLR (AD)28, we are of the view that there being a special limitation provided in the law, we are unable to condone the delay and admit the appeal as prayed for in the rule. In the aforesaid discussion, we find no merit in the rule. It is liable to be discharged.
